content.text:
Epic chosen: SMT-2 (Employee Profile, Skills & Certifications). Certificates belong to the employee profile, and nothing in the space covers expiry reminders yet. SMT-35 is a CSV download, so it doesn't overlap.

**Proposal: 1 Story, 4 Sub-tasks**

- Story: Email employees 30 days before a certificate expires (Epic SMT-2)
  - Sub-task: Backend: daily job to find certificates expiring in 30 days
  - Sub-task: Backend: email template and sending, with no duplicate reminders
  - Sub-task: Tests: reminder job and email sending
  - Sub-task: Documentation: certificate expiry reminder behaviour

I assumed three things. Tell me if any is wrong and I'll change the plan.
- Certificates already have an expiry date field.
- The email goes to the certificate owner only.
- It is sent once, exactly 30 days before expiry.

```plan
{"stories": [
  {"ref": "S1", "epic": "SMT-2", "summary": "Email employees 30 days before a certificate expires",
   "description": "Business context: Expired certificates leave skill records out of date and can block project eligibility. A timely reminder lets employees renew in time.

User story: As an employee, I want an email reminder 30 days before one of my certificates expires, so that I can renew it before it lapses.

Description: A daily scheduled check finds certificates whose expiry date is 30 days away and emails the owning employee once per certificate expiry date.

Acceptance criteria:
- An employee receives an email when one of their certificates is exactly 30 days from expiry.
- The email names the certificate and its expiry date.
- The same certificate expiry date never triggers more than one reminder.
- Certificates with no expiry date, or already expired, trigger no email.
- If the expiry date is changed (for example after renewal), a new reminder can be sent for the new date.",
   "subtasks": [
     {"summary": "Backend: daily job to find certificates expiring in 30 days",
      "description": "What to do: Add a scheduled daily job that selects certificates whose expiry date is today + 30 days and passes them to the email sender.

Dependencies: Certificate expiry date field on the employee profile.

Acceptance criteria:
- The job runs once per day.
- It selects only certificates expiring exactly 30 days from the run date.
- Certificates without an expiry date are skipped.
- A failure for one certificate does not stop the others.",
      "labels": ["backend"], "priority": "Medium"},
     {"summary": "Backend: reminder email template and sending, with no duplicate reminders",
      "description": "What to do: Create the reminder email (certificate name, expiry date, link to profile), send it to the owner, and record that the reminder was sent for that certificate and expiry date.

Dependencies: The daily job sub-task; the existing email or SMTP configuration.

Acceptance criteria:
- The email goes to the certificate owner and shows the certificate name and expiry date.
- A sent reminder is recorded per certificate and expiry date.
- Re-running the job on the same day sends no second email.
- A changed expiry date allows a new reminder.",
      "labels": ["backend", "email"], "priority": "Medium"},
     {"summary": "Tests: reminder job and email sending",
      "description": "What to do: Add unit tests for the job and the sender, using a fake email service.

Dependencies: The two backend sub-tasks.

Acceptance criteria:
- Tests cover a certificate exactly 30 days out, 29 and 31 days out, no expiry date, and already expired.
- Tests cover no duplicate send on re-run and a new send after the expiry date changes.
- Tests cover one failed send not blocking the others.",
      "labels": ["testing"], "priority": "Medium"},
     {"summary": "Documentation: certificate expiry reminder behaviour",
      "description": "What to do: Document when reminders are sent, who gets them, the email content and how the schedule is configured.

Dependencies: The backend sub-tasks.

Acceptance criteria:
- The documentation states the 30-day rule and the once-per-expiry-date rule.
- It explains how to configure or run the job.",
      "labels": ["documentation"], "priority": "Low"}
   ]}
]}
```

message.content: Keep it to one story with backend, frontend and Documentation sub-tasks

content.text:
Here is the updated proposal. It has 1 Story and 3 Sub-tasks, under SMT-2 (Employee Profile, Skills & Certifications) as before.

- Story: Email employees 30 days before a certificate expires
  - Sub-task: Backend: daily job and reminder email for certificates expiring in 30 days
  - Sub-task: Frontend: "expires soon" notice on the certificate list in the employee profile
  - Sub-task: Documentation: certificate expiry reminder behaviour

I folded the tests into the backend sub-task. I had to guess what the frontend work would be: a badge on the profile showing a certificate expires within 30 days. If you want something else there, tell me.

```plan
{"stories": [
  {"ref": "S1", "epic": "SMT-2", "summary": "Email employees 30 days before a certificate expires",
   "description": "Business context: Expired certificates leave skill records out of date and can block project eligibility. A timely reminder lets employees renew in time.

User story: As an employee, I want an email reminder 30 days before one of my certificates expires, so that I can renew it before it lapses.

Description: A daily scheduled check finds certificates whose expiry date is 30 days away and emails the owning employee once per certificate expiry date. The profile shows which certificates are close to expiry.

Acceptance criteria:
- An employee receives an email when one of their certificates is exactly 30 days from expiry.
- The email names the certificate and its expiry date.
- The same certificate expiry date never triggers more than one reminder.
- Certificates with no expiry date, or already expired, trigger no email.
- If the expiry date is changed (for example after renewal), a new reminder can be sent for the new date.
- The employee profile marks certificates that expire within 30 days.",
   "subtasks": [
     {"summary": "Backend: daily job and reminder email for certificates expiring in 30 days",
      "description": "What to do: Add a scheduled daily job that selects certificates whose expiry date is today + 30 days, emails the owner (certificate name, expiry date, link to profile) and records that the reminder was sent for that certificate and expiry date. Add unit tests using a fake email service.

Dependencies: Certificate expiry date field on the employee profile; existing email or SMTP configuration.

Acceptance criteria:
- The job runs once per day and selects only certificates expiring exactly 30 days from the run date.
- Certificates without an expiry date, or already expired, are skipped.
- The email goes to the certificate owner and shows the certificate name and expiry date.
- Re-running the job on the same day sends no second email.
- A changed expiry date allows a new reminder.
- A failed send for one certificate does not stop the others.
- Tests cover 29, 30 and 31 days out, no expiry date, already expired, no duplicate send, changed expiry date and a failed send.",
      "labels": ["backend", "email"], "priority": "Medium"},
     {"summary": "Frontend: expires-soon notice on the certificate list in the employee profile",
      "description": "What to do: Show a visible badge on each certificate that expires within 30 days, with the expiry date.

Dependencies: Certificate expiry date available from the profile API.

Acceptance criteria:
- Certificates expiring within 30 days show an expires-soon badge with the expiry date.
- Certificates with no expiry date, or expiring later, show no badge.
- Already expired certificates are shown as expired.",
      "labels": ["frontend"], "priority": "Low"},
     {"summary": "Documentation: certificate expiry reminder behaviour",
      "description": "What to do: Document when reminders are sent, who gets them, the email content, the profile badge and how the schedule is configured.

Dependencies: The backend and frontend sub-tasks.

Acceptance criteria:
- The documentation states the 30-day rule and the once-per-expiry-date rule.
- It explains how to configure or run the job.
- It describes the expires-soon badge.",
      "labels": ["documentation"], "priority": "Low"}
   ]}
]}
```
